Incident Overview: Three Queens Facebook (frequent video updates).The Three Queens Fire is located on Okanogan Wenatchee National Forest, six miles east of Snoqualmie Pass, in Kittitas County.   The Three Queens fire is burning primarily in high elevation subalpine fir stringers above Lake Kachess. Wind driven fire behavior persists as strong winds push flames across fuels. Fire activity has increased in areas where fuels, wind, and topography have aligned, producing periods of faster fire spread. This mountainous region also exhibits extreme slopes, unstable terrain and rolling material. Crews are monitoring these conditions closely and adjusting tactics to maintain safe and effective operations.EVACUATIONS: Kittitas County Sheriff’s Office has issued Level 3, 2, and 1 level evacuations.Current evacuation levels can be viewed on the Kittitas County Emergency Management live evacuation map here:https://experience.arcgis.com/.../cbd279e3569d45b4aeb28bc...Monitor the Kittitas County Sheriff's Facebook page for real-time updates https://www.facebook.com/KittitasCountySheriff.

Incident Overview: The Ross Fire in Palo Pinto County started on the afternoon of August 24, 2026 under elevated fire conditions. Texas A&M Forest Service was requested to provide assistance in the form of additional firefighters and heavy equipment at 12:41 pm and responded quickly. Texas A&M Forest Service is currently in unified command with local departments.Heavy equipment and aviation resources are assisting with suppression efforts. There is a Temporary Flight Restriction (TFR) in place for the area over the Ross Fire.  Please avoid the area to provide a safe environment for firefighting aircraft. [NOTAM: FDC 6/9626 https://tfr.faa.gov/tfr3/?page=detail_6_9626 ].  This are no evacuations at this time. Residents are strongly encouraged to continue checking on fire conditions and remain prepared to leave if needed.Please remain alert and be prepared for changing conditions. Additional information will be provided as it becomes available.

Incident Overview: The Grand Park 2 Fire was reported Aug. 7 and is located approximately three miles north of the Sunrise Visitor Center in Mount Rainier National Park. The Grand Park 2 Fire has now transitioned fully into patrol status, with containment lines continuing to be confirmed secure through aerial reconnaissance when available in this remote terrain. Firefighters finalized the backhaul from the Fir Tree Spike Camp and assisted with installing remote automated weather stations at both Suntop Lookout and Sunrise. Overhead personnel continued working through suppression‑repair tasks and used vantage points, including the Fremont Lookout, to track interior heat. No visible smoke was reported, and the fire showed no growth.

Incident Overview: WONDERLAND COMPLEX: 378 acres | 0% contained Across the Wonderland Complex, the hand crew, suppression module, and faller module completed thinning and cleanup around elite whitebark pine south of the Sunrise Visitor Center. The faller module also mitigated hazard trees around the Ranger Creek Forward Operating Base. Overhead and engines assisted with scouting additional values near the White River area, while personnel at Sunrise used the favorable conditions to clean up and organize equipment. Aerial reconnaissance showed increased smoke on all fires but no significant fire movement.On the Wonderland Complex, firefighters prepared pumps and supplies at Sunrise for expected rain and possible freezing temperatures. Personnel hiked to Fremont Lookout to track fire activity, while others backhauled waste barrels and bear boxes to designated sites in the park. Firefighters remain ready to respond should new starts emerge as weather begins to shift.
